title: A Summer for the Harbor
premise: Lior Montrose, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal ten years ago, returns to the coastal town of Harborlight to plan one last society wedding before quitting the business. The town's beloved anonymous pen-pal program, meant to pair lonely strangers, malfunctions and pairs Lior with his old rival — ferry captain Senna Voss, the woman who testified against his family a decade ago. Through letters neither knows are addressed to an enemy, they fall for each other's unguarded selves, until identities surface at the wedding itself. In the end, Lior must publicly speak the truth he rehearsed for ten years — that his family's ruin was his own doing, not hers — before boarding the last ferry of the season, where Senna either waits or doesn't.
about_author: Marguerite Ashgrove is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent three summers covering harbor festivals and ferry schedules before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who mistake pride for protection.

chapters.title: The Last Contract
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He arrives in Harborlight to plan the Whitmore wedding, his final job before abandoning weddings forever. A chance collision with Senna Voss at the dock revives a decade-old grudge on both sides. Emotional beat: armored cynicism masking dread of returning to the place where everything broke.

chapters.title: Letters in a Blue Box
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. The town librarian recruits both of them into the annual anonymous pen-pal program; a clerical error pairs them without names. Senna, lonely since selling her father's boat route, writes her first honest letter in years. Emotional beat: cautious hope she immediately distrusts.

chapters.title: Salt and Stationery
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. By day, Lior and Senna spar over wedding logistics — she's catering the event via her ferry-café; by night, their letters grow startlingly intimate. Each begins suspecting the other is someone they once loved. Emotional beat: the vertigo of liking your enemy.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A storm strands him at Senna's boathouse; they nearly connect as strangers-without-letters, but an old photograph of the trial surfaces and he retreats. He drafts a confession letter and burns it. Emotional beat: fear outrunning longing.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. Flashback chapter: ten years ago, young Senna told investigators what she saw the night the Montrose ferry company collapsed — believing she was helping, not destroying. Present-day, she recognizes Lior's phrasing in a letter and realizes who her pen pal is. Emotional beat: guilt re-igniting into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Truths, Unsent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both know now; neither says it. They keep writing anyway, each testing whether the other will confess first. The wedding preparations reach crisis point when the venue floods. Forced collaboration cracks something open between them. Emotional beat: complicity in shared silence.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Real Wounds
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the rehearsal dinner, a drunken groomsman toasts 'the woman who sank the Montroses,' exposing Senna's role to the room. Lior stays silent — and sees her face change. She leaves; the letters stop. Emotional beat: cowardice crystallizing into shame.

chapters.title: The Empty Dock
chapters.summary: Senna's POV. Senna decides to leave Harborlight on the last ferry of the season, done with towns that need scapegoats. Packing her father's letters, she finds proof she'd suppressed: evidence that Lior's father begged her to stay silent, and that Lior took the blame publicly to protect the crew. Emotional beat: grief rearranging into understanding.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Wedding day. Mid-ceremony, Lior abandons his notes and speaks the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade: 'It was my fault — I signed the manifest, and Senna Voss told the truth.' The room fractures; the bride, moved, tells him to run. He races for the last ferry. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: First Ferry of Forever
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Senna is on the departing ferry — having missed it deliberately, waiting at the rail. Lior leaps the gap as the gangplank rises. No speeches: just the sentence again, said plainly, and her hand closing around his. Epilogue beat: spring, a new ferry route co-signed by both their names. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.
